questions.prompt: What side effects does Buildgum actually perform today, and how reliable is each one?

keyPoints.text: The cart read from localStorage has no guard against corrupt data.
The cart write has no handling for quota or storage errors.
The checkout confirmation is pure UI state with no external effect behind it.
Nothing else leaves the browser: no network calls, messaging or background work of any kind.
keyPoints.quote: webhooks, email, queues, jobs, retries, cron, caches, workers

keyPoints.text: The localStorage read happens inside the cart state initializer.
A React effect persists every cart change back to localStorage.

questions.prompt: Explain the production-checkout reliability concepts the guide introduces - idempotency, retries, outbox, compensation, timeouts - and what each one prevents.

keyPoints.text: Idempotency means a repeated Pay now must not mint a second order.
keyPoints.quote: requests should not create duplicate orders

keyPoints.text: Today the button merely calls onComplete; a real checkout needs keys plus durable order state on the server.
keyPoints.quote: a real system needs idempotency keys and server-side order state

keyPoints.text: Transient payment, tax or fulfillment failures will be retried, and those retries have to be safe and observable.
keyPoints.quote: Retrying must be safe and observable.

keyPoints.text: The outbox pattern stores the intent to send a receipt atomically with the order, then delivers it asynchronously.
keyPoints.quote: persist the intent to send in the same transaction

keyPoints.text: Compensation handles the half-done case - license provisioned but email failed - with recovery instead of silent inconsistency.
keyPoints.quote: the system needs recovery, not silent inconsistency

keyPoints.text: Every external call needs a timeout and a clear failure state.
keyPoints.quote: need timeouts and clear failure states

keyPoints.text: Backpressure: admin dashboards must not issue unbounded queries or do expensive synchronous work.
keyPoints.quote: avoid unbounded queries and expensive synchronous work

questions.prompt: Where would a naive extension of this codebase go wrong, and how does the drill's checkout state machine guard against it?

keyPoints.text: Putting payment API calls straight into the Checkout component's render path is called out as incorrect.
keyPoints.quote: Adding payment API calls directly inside

keyPoints.text: Irreversible side effects do not belong in useEffect, because effects can run more than once.
keyPoints.quote: StrictMode and dependency changes can rerun effects

keyPoints.text: The client-computed subtotal must never be trusted for a real order.
keyPoints.quote: would be unsafe for real orders

keyPoints.text: That subtotal, discount and tax math lives in the Checkout component today.
The drill models checkout as explicit states from draft order through payment intent to receipt sent.
keyPoints.quote: draft order, payment intent, paid order, fulfillment pending, fulfilled, receipt sent

keyPoints.text: The exercise is to decide which state transitions have to be idempotent.
keyPoints.quote: Mark which transitions must be idempotent.
